title: Case report: severe lactic acidosis in a patient treated with metformin
abstract: A 44-year-old woman with acute kidney injury had been taking metformin (850 mg three times daily) for type 2 diabetes mellitus for 3 weeks. The patient was also receiving bisoprolol and ramipril. Several months later the patient developed severe lactic acidosis with profound malaise, abdominal pain and rapid deep breathing. Investigations pointed to septic shock. The event was judged unrelated to metformin and was attributed to septic shock. No recurrence was seen once the underlying cause had been treated.

title: Case report: lactic acidosis in a patient treated with Glucophage
abstract: A 49-year-old man with congestive heart failure had been taking Glucophage (850 mg three times daily) for type 2 diabetes mellitus for 6 months. Two days after the dose change, the patient presented with profound malaise, abdominal pain and rapid deep breathing and was diagnosed with lactic acidosis. Investigations showed arterial pH of 6.87 with serum lactate of 22.6 mmol/L. The drug was discontinued and the patient was admitted to intensive care for supportive management. The reaction was judged to be drug-related, with Glucophage the most likely cause. The patient recovered fully.

title: Case report: immune-mediated myositis in a patient treated with atorvastatin
abstract: A 42-year-old woman with prior coronary stenting had been taking atorvastatin (20 mg daily) for hypercholesterolaemia for 3 years. The patient was also receiving aspirin and pantoprazole. After starting aspirin, about a month later the patient presented with symmetrical proximal weakness persisting after statin withdrawal and was diagnosed with immune-mediated myositis while on atorvastatin. Investigations showed creatine kinase of 3520 U/L and anti-HMGCR antibodies. Atorvastatin was withdrawn; weakness improved slowly on corticosteroids. The event was considered probably related to atorvastatin. The patient recovered fully.

title: Case report: procedural haemorrhage in a patient treated with clopidogrel
abstract: A 42-year-old woman with anaemia had been taking clopidogrel (75 mg daily) for acute coronary syndrome with stent placement for 3 years. The patient was also receiving aspirin and amlodipine. Several months after the dose change, the patient presented with uncontrolled oozing after the dental extraction and was diagnosed with procedural haemorrhage. Causality assessment indicated a probable association with clopidogrel. The patient recovered fully.

abstract: A 51-year-old man with bipolar disorder had been taking olanzapine (15 mg at night) for schizophrenia for 3 weeks. title: Case report: neuroleptic malignant syndrome in a patient treated with olanzapine
abstract: A 43-year-old man with no significant comorbidity had been taking olanzapine (20 mg daily) for schizophrenia for 2 months. The patient was also receiving bisoprolol and aspirin. Two days after the dose change, the patient presented with fever, diaphoresis, tremor and autonomic instability and was diagnosed with neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Investigations showed creatine kinase rising to 22476 U/L with leucocytosis and temperature 40.3 C. Olanzapine was withdrawn and the patient was managed in the intensive care unit. Causality assessment indicated a probable association with olanzapine. The patient recovered fully.

title: Case report: immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy in a patient treated with atorvastatin
abstract: A 42-year-old man with type 2 diabetes had been taking atorvastatin (40 mg daily) for hypercholesterolaemia for 10 days. One week after the dose change, the patient presented with difficulty climbing stairs and persistent muscle pain and was diagnosed with immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy. Investigations showed creatine kinase of 6102 U/L and anti-HMGCR antibodies. Atorvastatin was stopped and the patient was treated with prednisolone and intravenous immunoglobulin. Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy was attributed to atorvastatin. The patient recovered fully.

title: Case report: procedural haemorrhage in a patient treated with Plavix
abstract: A 65-year-old woman with prior gastrointestinal bleed had been taking Plavix (75 mg daily) for acute coronary syndrome with stent placement for 3 weeks. The patient was also receiving lisinopril. About a month after the dose change, the patient presented with persistent bleeding from the access site and was diagnosed with procedural haemorrhage. Investigations showed a haemoglobin drop from 13.6 to 7.8 g/dL. The antiplatelet was held and local haemostatic measures were applied. Procedural haemorrhage was attributed to Plavix. The patient recovered fully.

title: Case report: lactic acidosis in a patient treated with metformin
abstract: A 81-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease stage 4 had been taking metformin (850 mg three times daily) for type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 months. One week after the dose change, the patient presented with severe myalgia, hypotension and drowsiness and was diagnosed with lactic acidosis. Investigations showed arterial pH of 6.98 with serum lactate of 9.5 mmol/L. Metformin was stopped and bicarbonate infusion with renal replacement therapy was started. Causality assessment indicated a probable association with metformin. The patient recovered fully.
